notes: Summary: Building a VS Code copilot extension for internal and paid tiers; primary goal is low-latency inline completions and reliable streaming token delivery.
Org size: ~420 engs, distributed US + EMEA, heavy use of monorepo and internal toolchains.
Primary ask: sub-100ms per-token streaming for inline suggestions in editor; end-to-end (client -> Redwood -> model) p95 target < 120ms for short completions.
Prefers pinned model versions per release channel (stable/beta). Wants ability to pin both model and quantization profile per route.
Auth: SSO/SAML for corporate accounts, per-dev API keys for local testing, audit logs for every generation request; KMS integration for key wrapping.
Rate limiting: need per-user and per-team quotas; burst behaviour when entire org types during standups is a concern.
Data residency: source code never leaves customer region for enterprise tier; evaluating Dedicated or Private for higher trust customers.
Workflows: offline dev (local LSP fallback) + cloud streaming for telemetry and better quality; want automatic fallback to local small model when network degraded.
Cost sensitivity: high at scale — estimate 400 devs using daily 2k tokens avg; asks for batching/caching suggestions to reduce unit cost.
Observability: wants token-level cost dashboards, per-route latency breakdown, and trace linking from editor sessions to Redwood Console.
Quote from VP Eng: 'We need completions that feel instant — anything slower than the editor baseline frustrates devs.'
Demo notes (02/14 call): showed VS Code extension prototype using Redwood streaming API; extension uses WebSocket for continuous token stream + fallback polling for older clients.
Tech notes: extension keeps an LRU prompt cache per repo to reduce repeated context costs; tests show 2-3x cost savings on repeated snippet suggestions.
Security review status: answered Security FAQ; SOC2 report requested; legal sent DPA redlines 02/28.
POC asks: 2-week POC with 50 power users, synthetic perf tests (100 concurrent completions), access to Redwood Console for telemetry, a canary model pin for stable channel.
Internal decision criteria: latency, streaming stability, price per 1M tokens, SSO + audit capabilities, ease of rollout via extension marketplace.
Assoc assets: extension prototype repo (private), summit slides (Jan 2026) where they introduced the copilot product to beta customers.
AE notes: keep pricing conversation separate until POC shows latency baselines; recommend Dedicated pool for predictable throughput if >200 concurrent streams.
SE notes: Diego to run perf harness w/ Redwood dedicated-config (g4x-like) to validate p95 targets; ask Redwood for kernel/quantization recommendations for pinned model.
CSM notes: Priya for onboarding checklist and success metrics if POC succeeds (adoption %, CSAT, cost per active dev).
